svg.title: What's published, what's argued, what's unmeasured
svg.desc: Evidence ledger. Published: the cost-driver formula, computed at scale [1, 2]; attribution coverage and residuals [2] (tracing 52% of capacity usage in 2022; residuals of 3 to 5% for a stateless web product and 22% falling to 15% for databases), still open for stateful services and batched inference; and the nearest results on the mechanisms, parts safety stock at about 0.6 times under triangulation [8] and planning cut from three to four months to about one [34]. Published in part: lead times by layer [6, 8, 60–64, 109]; how long large new loads wait for power, on which little is published [65]; uncertainty at a commit point, with observational evidence only, a 2x difference in machine count forecasts [8]; and the pieces of the thirteen mechanisms [8, 31, 34]. Published in part, too: the slow end of the cover point rising with lead time [8]. Argued here: the cover point rising with lead time, not a published result; the thirteen mechanisms joined, argued from practice; and the commit-point method, untested. Not found in public sources: order-to-dock times, turn-up durations, hardware contract terms, coefficient drift over time and how often coefficients are recalibrated, how well declarations are calibrated by stage and how often launches slip, and mechanisms for arbitrating scarce accelerators between internal and external demand (one preprint covers internal teams only [18]; operators state splits and priority orders, not mechanisms [90, 102]). The tests of Section 9.2 have not been run. A footer says not found means in the sources the author could read, including the second edition of Site Reliability Engineering's capacity chapter [7].
